facts.value: English 105 is a one-semester course that practices the various ways of reading and writing that are studied in English 101 as well as the research and argumentation strategies that are studied in English 102. The pace is faster so the workload is heavier.

metadata.chunk_title: What is English 105? + Are there any awards, publications, or honors I might be eligible for through Writing Programs? + What is the policy for adding or dropping a Writing Programs course? + Course Withdrawal Deadlines + May I get an override to enroll in a closed section?

facts.value: You may qualify for placement into English 105 by: an ACT score of 26 or more; an SAT score of 660 or more (620 or more if taken before 2016); an Accuplacer score of 8 (8-point system, effective Fall 2009)/11 or above (12-point system prior to Fall 2009); Either of these two CLEP test scores: English Composition with essay -- the General Examination, a score of 610/1978 scale or 500/1986 scale or more; Freshman College Composition -- the Subject Examination, a score of 50 or more.
